::: {.why}
Shrinkage improves an estimate by pulling it toward a shape; a factor model asserts the shape, which needs far fewer parameters and is wrong in ways you can name.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Build a covariance matrix from factor exposures and idiosyncratic variances, and count its parameters against the sample matrix.
- Name the assumption a factor covariance makes that your residual correlation matrix shows is false.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Build it: with K factors, the covariance is the exposure matrix times the factor covariance times its transpose plus a diagonal of residual variances. Implement it for a market-plus-sector model on your 200 names and count the parameters against the sample matrix's.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Test the assumption you just made: the model asserts residuals are uncorrelated across names. Use last night's residual correlation matrix to measure how false that is, report the average absolute off-diagonal, and identify the structure the model is missing.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add the factor estimator to qlib/risk.py's interface so it is selectable like the others.
:::
:::
